newsitem.title: USA: USDA orange crop estimate neutral for FCOJ futures.
newsitem.headline: USDA orange crop estimate neutral for FCOJ futures.

text.p: U.S. Agriculture Department's 1996/97 Florida orange crop estimate released Thursday morning was mostly neutral and should have little effect on FCOJ futures, analysts said.
"The report was expected to be a non-event and that is how it came in," said Paine Webber analyst Bernard Savaiko.
USDA pegged 1996/97 Florida's crop at 220 million 90-lb boxes, unchanged from its December forecast but up eight percent from a year ago.

The agency also let stand its Florida frozen concentrated orange juice yield estimate for the 1996/97 season at 1.53 gallons per box at 42.0 degrees Brix, although some analysts had anticipated a revision upward from the December forecast.
"The report was neutral to a bit positive," said Celeste Georgakis, FCOJ specialist at Dean Witter. "It might be viewed as contructive since people expected an upward revision on yields."

UDSA also forecast all U.S. orange production in 1996/97 at a record high 12.5 million tons, up one percent from last month's estimate and five percent higher than the previous record 11.8 million tons tons set in the 1979/80 season.
